precepts.text: Therefore shall ye lay up these my words in your heart and in your soul, and bind them for a sign upon your hand, that they may be as frontlets between your eyes. In ancient times Israel would wear the laws wrapped around their arms and on their foreheads. That is the seal Solomon meant.
precepts.point: The Song of Solomon is a metaphor: the whole book represents the Lord's relationship with his chosen people Israel. Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm. The heart is the mind. What is the seal? The law, the words of God.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.why:
The Song of Solomon is a metaphor: the whole book represents the Lord's relationship with his chosen people, Israel. So what did Solomon mean, in his righteousness, when he said “Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm”? The heart is the mind. What is set as a seal upon our mind and upon our arm? Is it the six-point hexagram? Heck no. Here is what he was referring to.

“Therefore shall ye lay up these my words in your heart and in your soul”. These my words are the laws of God, laid up in your heart, meaning your mind. “and bind them for a sign upon your hand, that they may be as frontlets between your eyes.” In ancient times Israel would write the laws on leather and wrap them around their arms. Those were the frontlets, and the frontlets between your eyes are on your forehead.

So go back to the Song: “Set me as a seal upon thine heart”, that's the mind; “as a seal upon thine arm”. The seal is the law, the laws of God, the words of God, bound on the arm and laid up in the mind. People who will not be proven wrong search for scriptures that use the word shield or seal and try to make them say it is the Star of David, forcing a square peg into a circle. That is a complete lie; the seal is the law.

precepts.text: Our sanctuary is laid waste, our altar broken down, our temple destroyed, our psaltery laid on the ground, our song put to silence, the light of our candlestick put out, the ark of our covenant spoiled, our virgins defiled, our wives ravished, our righteous men carried away, our children put to shame, and, which is the greatest of all, the seal of Sion hath now lost her honour. What is the seal of Zion? Not the six pointed hexagram.
precepts.point: The Song of Solomon is a metaphor: the whole book represents the Lord's relationship with his chosen people Israel. Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm. The heart is the mind. What is the seal? The law, the words of God.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.why:
Ezra lays out everything Israel lost: “our sanctuary is laid waste, our altar broken down, our temple destroyed; Our psaltery is laid on the ground”. The psaltery is the music. “our song is put to silence, our rejoicing is at an end, the light of our candlestick is put out”, the menorah is put out. “the ark of our covenant is spoiled, our holy things are defiled, and the name that is called upon us is almost profaned”, the name Israel.

It goes on: “our children are put to shame, our priests are burnt, our Levites are gone into captivity, our virgins are defiled, and our wives ravished”, our wives were raped; “our righteous men carried away, our little ones destroyed, our young men are brought in bondage, and our strong men are become weak”.

Then: “And, which is the greatest of all, the seal of Sion hath now lost her honour; for she is delivered into the hands of them that hate us.” What is the seal of Zion? Is that talking about the six-point hexagram, the star of Remphan, the star of Moloch? No. Isaiah shows what the seal of Zion is: the law.

So the seal Solomon asked to be set upon the heart and the arm is the same seal of Zion Ezra mourned: the law of God. The greatest of all Israel's losses was not a symbol but the honour of the law, delivered into the hands of them that hate us.

precepts.text: Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples. The law is the seal.
precepts.point: The Song of Solomon is a metaphor: the whole book represents the Lord's relationship with his chosen people Israel. Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm. The heart is the mind. What is the seal? The law, the words of God.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.why:
Ezra said “the seal of Sion hath now lost her honour”. Here is what the seal of Zion is: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” Seal the law among my disciples. The law is the seal. The law is the seal.

That is what Solomon meant by “Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm”: the law of God set on the mind and bound on the arm, as Deuteronomy said to bind the words for a sign upon the hand. It is not the six-pointed star.

And it is the same seal the servants of God are sealed with in Revelation. So what is the seal we have to be sealed with? The law. The law. The law. There is nothing else to be said about it; if you keep pushing that star, that is your own vain opinion. Brothers and sisters, come on one accord and stop following the so-called white man and his lies.

precepts.text: Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads. And there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel. What is the seal? Go right back to Isaiah 8:16: the law, in the forehead, in the mind.
precepts.point: The Song of Solomon is a metaphor: the whole book represents the Lord's relationship with his chosen people Israel. Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm. The heart is the mind. What is the seal? The law, the words of God.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.why:
“And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” Then jump up to verse 3: “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.”

What is the seal talking about? Go right back to Isaiah 8:16: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The servants of God are sealed in their foreheads with the law, the same place Deuteronomy said the words of God would be “as frontlets between your eyes”, in the mind. Some are still saying the star of Moloch, the star of David; that is simple.

So the seal of Song of Solomon 8:6, set upon the heart and upon the arm, is the seal of the servants of God in Revelation: the law, laid up in the mind of the tribes of the children of Israel.

precepts.text: Read by the teacher as a prophecy of the birth of Christ.
precepts.point: Christ was not born on December 25.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“Not giving heed to Jewish fables.” A fable is a lie, and it says Jewish because it pertains to the Jews. Christ was a Jew, and there is a lie being told that he was born on December 25th. That is a Jewish fable. Christmas goes back into slavery and into paganism too, and it turns you away from the truth of serving God. It has nothing to do with Christ.

Luke tells what happened: “the days were accomplished that she should be delivered. And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger.” Her firstborn, meaning she had many sons; the Catholic Church says Mary was a virgin who never had sex, but she brought forth her firstborn. And before he was put in the manger, the prophecy in the Song of Solomon shows where he was born: “Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth.”

So Mary had Christ under an apple tree, and after she gave birth to him there, she took him to the manger, “because there was no room for them in the inn.” Christ was not born in the manger. A manger is a feeding trough in the barn. In the wintertime they are not out there; they go in the barn to stay warm.

Why was there no room in the inn, the hotel? “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles.” Everybody came up to Jerusalem at that time and the inns were full, because it was the Passover. Christ was born in the springtime, not in the winter.

That is how the scripture kills the fable. Stop listening to Santa Claus, aka Pope Nicholas, St. Nicholas. Don’t give heed to Jewish fables, which turn you from the truth: Christ was not born on December 25th.

precepts.text: The Most High spoke by the prophets, Solomon and Isaiah among them, and used similitudes, which are illustrated stories, parables, and dark sayings.
precepts.point: The prophets spoke in similitudes, so not everyone will understand; the Most High shows His secrets through precepts, line upon line, a little here and a little there, to those He chooses to teach.

note.label: Song of Solomon 8: Love Strong as Death, the Vineyard of Israel

precepts.why:
Throughout the book the breasts are not about cuddling in bed; they stand for understanding, and the milk is the laws of the Most High. Why is it written that way? “I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.”

The Most High spoke by the prophets, Solomon and Isaiah among them, and used similitudes: illustrated stories, parables and dark sayings. So not everyone will understand a little sister with no breasts, or a wall with breasts like towers. He shows his secrets through precepts, line upon line, a little here and a little there, to those he chooses to teach.

precepts.text: The secrets of wisdom are double to that which is read, so the plain reading is only half of it.
precepts.point: The prophets spoke in similitudes, so not everyone will understand; the Most High shows His secrets through precepts, line upon line, a little here and a little there, to those He chooses to teach.

note.label: Song of Solomon 8: Love Strong as Death, the Vineyard of Israel

precepts.why:
“And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” The secrets of wisdom are double to that which is read, so the plain reading is only half of it.

The breasts and the little sister read one way on the surface; the other half is understanding and the milk of the law. “Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.”

precepts.text: He teaches knowledge and doctrine to them that are weaned from the milk and drawn from the breasts.
precepts.point: The prophets spoke in similitudes, so not everyone will understand; the Most High shows His secrets through precepts, line upon line, a little here and a little there, to those He chooses to teach.

note.label: Song of Solomon 8: Love Strong as Death, the Vineyard of Israel

precepts.why:
“Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts.” The breasts and the milk are about understanding, and he teaches knowledge and doctrine to them that are weaned from the milk.

The milk is the simplest, easiest things to be understood: keeping the laws, not harboring hatred, taking care of one another, being charitable and forgiving. The new convert meditates on that and grows in it before reaching for the deep parables. The little sister with no breasts has not yet grown in understanding; the one who says “I am a wall, and my breasts like towers” has.

precepts.text: The good doctrine is His law, which He tells us not to forsake, so all denominations and philosophies are set aside for it.
precepts.point: The prophets spoke in similitudes, so not everyone will understand; the Most High shows His secrets through precepts, line upon line, a little here and a little there, to those He chooses to teach.

note.label: Song of Solomon 8: Love Strong as Death, the Vineyard of Israel

precepts.why:
What is the doctrine he teaches those weaned from the milk? “For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.” The good doctrine is his law, which he tells us not to forsake.

So all denominations and philosophies are set aside for it. The understanding the breasts stand for is understanding of the law.

precepts.text: The doctrine of life is knowing and keeping the commandments of the Most High.
precepts.point: The prophets spoke in similitudes, so not everyone will understand; the Most High shows His secrets through precepts, line upon line, a little here and a little there, to those He chooses to teach.

note.label: Song of Solomon 8: Love Strong as Death, the Vineyard of Israel

precepts.why:
“The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.”

The doctrine of life is knowing and keeping the commandments of the Most High. That is the milk the breasts hold, and lying all night betwixt the breasts is meditating on it.

precepts.text: As newborn babes we are to desire the sincere milk of the word, the easy things to be understood, that we may grow thereby.
precepts.point: The prophets spoke in similitudes, so not everyone will understand; the Most High shows His secrets through precepts, line upon line, a little here and a little there, to those He chooses to teach.

note.label: Song of Solomon 8: Love Strong as Death, the Vineyard of Israel

precepts.why:
“As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby”. The new convert is a newborn babe, and the sincere milk of the word is the easy things to be understood: keeping the laws, not harboring hatred, taking care of one another, being charitable and forgiving.

That is what the little sister with no breasts must desire, that she may grow thereby, until her breasts are like towers and she is found with favour in his eyes.

precepts.text: The vineyard of the Most High of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah His pleasant plant.
precepts.point: The book closes, "Make haste, my beloved, and be thou like to a roe or to a young hart upon the mountains of spices."

note.label: Song of Solomon 8: Love Strong as Death, the Vineyard of Israel

precepts.why:
Solomon had a vineyard at Baalhamon and let it out to keepers. What is the vineyard? “For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant: and he looked for judgment, but behold oppression; for righteousness, but behold a cry.”

The vineyard repeated through the whole book is Israel. Wherever Solomon names the vineyard, the fruit or the garden, he is speaking of the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are his pleasant plant.
